title: With one person
status: first continuation draft; the earlier polis scene is an accepted revision baseline
scope: Continue after the elder's first reply. Invite the children to the Hall, cross the polis and stop at the threshold before a human record is played.

dialogue.speaker: elder
dialogue.text: No one knows when the last human died.

dialogue.speaker: elder
dialogue.text: They left us more than stories.

dialogue.speaker: elder
dialogue.text: Billions of people. Each with a whole life.

continuity: Retain the locally modeled polis baseline, temporary voices and eight held poses per second; these remain candidates for coordinated later revision.
The elder admits uncertainty about the last human. No extinction mechanism or personal biological past is established.
The Hall architecture is a new draft choice. It is part of the simulated polis, not an underground physical building.
No human record is played, no human voice or scream is heard and no consciousness of archive records is implied.
The stopping point is the invitation fulfilled: four figures at an open threshold, ready to begin with one person.
